subject: Dedicated capacity: reserve scenarios, GPU tradeoffs, and $/1M token targets
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Patrick Nguyen <patrick@helixdata.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: reserve scenarios, GPU tradeoffs, and $/1M token targets

Hi Patrick —

Thanks again for the run-through this morning. Quick recap and the concrete asks we promised to follow up on:

1) Target throughput & economics you gave today
   - 700 concurrent requests, median response ~350 tokens, peak QPS ~60 (expected burst to 120)
   - Current cost target: <$6.50 per 1M tokens for prediction workload (inference only)

2) Questions we said we'd land by EOD:
   - H100 vs A100 trade: latency & per-token cost delta for your median sequence length
   - Reserved GPU sizing options we recommend for both your steady-state and burst patterns (3-variant worksheet attached)
   - Estimated unit $/1M tokens under each reserve band (3k, 6k, 12k reserved lane equivalence)

Attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing-v2.xlsx (worksheet: HelixData scenarios) and helix-throughput-estimates.pdf (breakdown of your sample traces we used).

Next steps:
- I’ll set a 30-min follow-up for early next week to run the worksheet with your finance/procurement and map to a commit you’re comfortable with.
- Karthik: can you add per-GPU latency numbers for the 8k/16k context lengths and the quantized-16-bit run we discussed?

Patrick — if the $/1M target above is out of band, tell us the ballpark budget range you’d accept and we’ll show which reserve option meets it.

Thanks,
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), helix-throughput-estimates.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Patrick Nguyen <patrick@helixdata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: reserve scenarios, GPU tradeoffs, and $/1M token targets

LAuren / Patrick — adding the requested performance data. Key bullets from the benchmarks (attached as a quick table in the spreadsheet):

- H100 (80GB, FP16)
  - median token latency: 6.2 ms/token at 8k context, continuous steady batching
  - cost per GPU-hour (estimate with reserved pricing): $5.40
  - effective $/1M tokens (model: 7B-ish, your trace): ~$5.10 (steady state, with KV cache)

- A100 (40GB, FP16)
  - median token latency: 8.9 ms/token at 8k context
  - cost per GPU-hour: $3.90
  - effective $/1M tokens: ~$7.40 (higher token cost due to throughput ceiling and increased batching inefficiency)

Sizing guidance (quick):
- Reserve band A (conservative steady): 6 GPUs H100 (predicts ~50–60k tokens/s aggregate) — best latency headroom for your bursts, $/1M ~ $5.6
- Reserve band B (balanced): 4 H100 + 2 A100 (mixed lane) — cheaper commit, $/1M ~ $6.0, still covers median with controlled burst to 100 QPS using autoscale burst lanes
- Reserve band C (cost-first): 8 A100 — lowers monthly commit but pushes $/1M toward $7.1 under your median workload

I put the full micro-bench numbers and the math in the spreadsheet. If you want, we can run a quick sensitivity scenario: decrease average tokens/respond by 10% (optimistic) and show the delta to $/1M.

Karthik
Senior SE, Redwood Inference

From: Patrick Nguyen <patrick@helixdata.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixdata.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: reserve scenarios, GPU tradeoffs, and $/1M token targets

Thanks Lauren & Karthik — helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- We were trying to hit a ceiling of $6 / 1M tokens (inference only). Seeing H100 steady at ~$5.1 looks promising, but that assumes sustained batching that we may not achieve for some routes (low-latency customer-facing calls).
- For low-latency interactive routes we need 99th pct latency < 400ms end-to-end; can you confirm that 6 H100s give that margin during 2x burst?
- Procurement question: what is minimum commit term for the reserve bands, and do you offer a trial band with buy-down credits if we convert to a larger commit within 90 days?

Also looping in our procurement team; they want a simple worksheet that maps monthly commit -> expected $/1M token and the cancellation/upgrade terms.

Patrick
Head of AI Platform, HelixData

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Patrick Nguyen <patrick@helixdata.com>, procurement@helixdata.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: reserve scenarios, GPU tradeoffs, and $/1M token targets

Patrick — good questions. Quick answers and a proposed commit worksheet (see attached spreadsheet, tab: "Commit-opts"):

- 99th pct latency: Karthik validated the 2x burst headroom; with 6 H100 and our autoscale policy (2 warm spare burst lanes) we see 99th token latency < 350ms for your sample traces. I'll paste the conservative 99th numbers into the spreadsheet comments.
- Commit terms: standard reserved term is 12 months. We can offer a 6-month pilot at a slightly higher per-GPU rate or a 12-month commit with a 90-day upgrade path and buy-down credit for any additional committed spend (details in the sheet).
- Trial band option: we can do a 6-month pilot (3 H100 equiv) with a conversion credit equal to 40% of what you paid toward a 12-month commit if you convert within 90 days of pilot end. That preserves runway for you while keeping pricing predictable.

Next steps I propose:
1) Can procurement confirm whether a 6-month pilot with conversion credit is acceptable? (procurement@helixdata.com)
2) If yes, we’ll schedule a 30-min finance sync to populate real month-on-month token forecasts into the worksheet (I suggest Mon/Tue next week)

If you prefer, we can also produce a conservative "low-latency route" carve-out: keep 2 H100 reserved solely for interactive traffic (hard SLA) and the rest pooled for batch/async — the spreadsheet shows the delta to $/1M for that split.

Thanks,
Lauren
